checks: Positive ambient volume of each slab makes the outer slices compact full-dimensional convex bodies. Their Minkowski midpoint lies in the middle slab. Brunn–Minkowski in ambient dimension r+1 gives equality and positive homothety. Equal volume makes the outer slabs translates. A strict closed convex inclusion between bodies would leave a positive-volume region, so the midpoint equals the middle slab as a set.

Writing the projection as [alpha,beta], the slab translation and midpoint left endpoint respectively give q_t=2-alpha, beta=3-alpha and 1=1+alpha/2. This fixes the full projection to [0,3] and the unit translation to (v,1), including the endpoint fibers.

For every support direction the detrended section support is concave and 1-periodic. Interpolation on [0,1] gives the lower bound at a; interpolating 1 between 0 and 1+a gives the reverse bound. Periodicity gives constancy on [0,3]. Positive integrated volume makes the resulting fixed cross-section full dimensional.

The classical convex-body inequality and equality statement are independently documented by Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski Inequality, equation (1) and §6, https://faculty.gardner.wwu.edu/gorizia12.pdf. The application here is to two positive-volume convex bodies at interpolation weight one half.

overlap.comparison: Its proof (3)–(4) uses the same equality mechanism for equal-volume sampled fibers to obtain their translates at integer same-parity midpoints. It does not conclude that all levels of an ordinary three-slab body are one affine shear.

readability: The proof and its scope are clear.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Equal positive outer-slab volumes force equality in the midpoint inclusion, then the section shear is rigid on the full interval.
